subject: Archaeology
title: Scanning the Pyramids with Technology
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Scanning the Pyramids with Technology.

hook.text: Robots, drones, and cosmic rays are exploring parts of Egyptian monuments that humans cannot reach.

buildup.text: The ScanPyramids project used muon detectors to image the Great Pyramid's interior without touching it.

discovery.text: They confirmed a 100-foot void above the Grand Gallery — a space unseen since the pyramid was sealed.

twist.text: Tiny robots sent up shafts in the Queen's Chamber found doors with copper handles. What is behind them remains unknown.

climax.text: Thermal imaging detected heat anomalies in the pyramid walls, hinting at more undiscovered chambers.

punchline.text: The oldest wonder of the ancient world is still giving up new secrets.

quiz.question: What did the ScanPyramids project discover inside the Great Pyramid?
options: A hidden burial chamber containing a second sarcophagus
A 100-foot void above the Grand Gallery
Underground tunnels connecting the three main Giza pyramids

details.summary: Modern technology has revealed hidden chambers and passages inside the pyramids without drilling. Muon tomography, thermal imaging, and ground-penetrating radar have detected voids in the Great Pyramid, reigniting debates about undiscovered rooms and construction techniques.
details.whyItMatters: Non-invasive scanning lets archaeologists explore sealed structures without damaging them. The discovery of a large void inside the Great Pyramid in 2017 shows that major discoveries remain possible in the most studied monuments on Earth.
takeaways: Muon tomography detected a large void in the Great Pyramid
Thermal imaging reveals construction differences in stone blocks
Non-invasive methods enable exploration without damage

faq.question: How does muon tomography work on pyramids?
faq.answer: Cosmic ray muons pass through stone at different rates depending on density. By placing detectors inside the pyramid and measuring incoming muon patterns, scientists can map internal density variations, revealing voids and chambers hidden within the stone mass.

faq.question: What was the void discovered in 2017?
faq.answer: The ScanPyramids project detected a large void at least 30 meters long above the Grand Gallery in the Great Pyramid of Khufu. Its purpose remains unknown — it could be a construction feature, a relieving chamber, or an undiscovered room.
